(* Relocate anchors and search snippets using unique shingles and local alignment.

   Normalize whitespace before extracting shingles. Ignore repeated shingles
   in both queries and documents. Index documents at stride 8 and query at
   stride 1.

   Require at least half the query's unique shingles, adjusted for the index
   stride, before considering a document. Select hits within 500 raw bytes
   of the most frequent query-minus-document offset. Choose the smallest
   offset on frequency ties. Align the original query bytes against the
   selected document window with Smith-Waterman. Whitespace gaps are free;
   other gaps cost one and substitutions cost two. Require the final
   range to span at least half the original query length after whitespace
   normalization of both strings.

   Failed attempts preserve anchor content and advance only the attempted
   revision. Successful attempts update both revision fields. Other edited
   documents may still have their previous indexed contents.
*)

open Printf
module T = App_types.Text

type doc_id = T.doc_id
type anchor_status = Up_to_date of Util.Text_source.t | Outdated

type anchor = {
  anchor_id : T.anchor_id;
  doc_id : T.doc_id;
  source_doc : T.source_doc;
  range : T.range;
  raw_contents : string;
  last_author : T.author;
  status : anchor_status;
  needs_review : bool;
}

module Set = Set.Make (struct
  type t = anchor

  let compare a b = compare a.anchor_id b.anchor_id
end)

(* Shingle length in normalized bytes.

   The 16-byte length and 8-byte stride balance index size and relocation
   accuracy on this repository. Whitespace normalization makes shingles
   denser and less sensitive to reindentation. See the borderline matching
   cases in [tests/Text_api_tests.ml] for accuracy checks. *)
let shingle_length = 16

(* Distance between indexed shingles, in normalized bytes. Adjacent
   shingles overlap by [shingle_length - shingle_offset] bytes.
   Queries use a stride of one byte. *)
let shingle_offset = 8

(* Allow up to 500 raw bytes of displacement on either side of the mode. *)
let match_offset_tolerance = 500

(* Minimum normalized anchor length needed to produce a query shingle.
   [add_anchor] also uses this as an early check on the raw byte length. *)
let min_anchor_length = shingle_length

(* Limit accidental whole-file anchors and their storage and matching cost.
   This fixed limit is separate from the configurable indexing file limit. *)
let max_anchor_length = 10 * 1024

(* A query needs at least one shingle after whitespace normalization. *)
let min_query_length = shingle_length

let get_doc_meta_exn db (src_doc : App_types.Src_doc.t) =
  let source_doc = App_types.Src_doc.to_source_doc src_doc in
  match
    DB.Documents.get_by_locator db ~source:source_doc.source
      source_doc.locator
  with
  | Some meta -> meta
  | None ->
      ksprintf failwith "Not indexed: %s" (App_types.Src_doc.show src_doc)

let to_public_anchor db (a : Internal_types.anchor) : anchor =
  let doc_meta, contents =
    match DB.Documents.get_full_by_id db a.doc_id with
    | Some x -> x
    | None -> failwith "Anchor references a nonexistent document"
  in
  (* Every edit must reconcile all anchors still on the document.
     Successful relocation advances both revision fields. Failure advances
     only [doc_revision_attempt]. A mismatch here violates that invariant. *)
  if a.doc_revision_attempt <> doc_meta.revision then
    ksprintf failwith
      "internal error: anchor %s's doc_revision_attempt (%d) does not match \
       document %s's revision (%d)"
      (App_types.Anchor_id.to_string a.anchor_id)
      a.doc_revision_attempt
      (App_types.Src_doc.show_source_doc doc_meta.source_doc)
      doc_meta.revision;
  let status =
    match contents with
    | DB.Deleted ->
        (* A deleted document cannot provide current context. *)
        Outdated
    | DB.Active contents ->
        if a.doc_revision = doc_meta.revision then
          Up_to_date
            { Util.Text_source.name = doc_meta.source_doc.locator; contents }
        else Outdated
  in
  let needs_review =
    match status with
    | Up_to_date _ -> false
    | Outdated -> (
        match a.acknowledged_revision with
        | None -> true
        | Some r -> r < doc_meta.revision)
  in
  {
    anchor_id = a.anchor_id;
    doc_id = a.doc_id;
    source_doc = doc_meta.source_doc;
    range = a.range;
    raw_contents = a.raw_contents;
    last_author = a.last_author;
    status;
    needs_review;
  }

(* Whitespace normalization                                             *)

(* TODO: Consider Unicode code point coordinates to avoid splitting UTF-8
   characters into shingles. Inputs can still contain invalid UTF-8, and
   public byte ranges would need conversion. *)

(* Share normalization and its position map with [Slice] text matching. *)
type normalized = Util.Text.normalized = {
  text : string;
  norm_to_raw : int array;
}

let normalize_whitespace = Util.Text.normalize_whitespace

(* Map both boundaries through [norm_to_raw]. A normalized space can span
   multiple raw whitespace bytes. *)
let raw_range_of_normalized (n : normalized) ~start ~end_ : T.range =
  let start, end_ = Util.Text.raw_range_of_normalized n ~start ~end_ in
  { T.start; end_ }

(* Shingle extraction                                                    *)

(* Ignore every occurrence of a repeated shingle, including its first one.
   Keep encounter order so extraction is deterministic. *)
let iter_shingles ~offset text f =
  let counts = Hashtbl.create 128 in
  let shingles = ref [] in
  for i = 0 to max (-1) (String.length text - shingle_length) do
    if i mod offset = 0 then begin
      let shingle = String.sub text i shingle_length in
      Hashtbl.replace counts shingle
        (1 + Option.value (Hashtbl.find_opt counts shingle) ~default:0);
      shingles := (i, shingle) :: !shingles
    end
  done;
  List.rev !shingles
  |> List.iter (fun (i, shingle) ->
      if Hashtbl.find counts shingle = 1 then f i shingle)

let index_shingles db ~doc_id contents =
  let n = normalize_whitespace contents in
  iter_shingles ~offset:shingle_offset n.text (fun norm_start shingle ->
      let range =
        raw_range_of_normalized n ~start:norm_start
          ~end_:(norm_start + shingle_length)
      in
      DB.Shingles.add db ~doc_id
        ~shingle:(Internal_types.Shingle_str.create shingle)
        ~range)

(* Each query shingle has one raw offset and at most one indexed occurrence
   per document. *)
type hit = {
  anchor_offset : int;
  query_start : int;
  doc_start : int;
  doc_end : int;
}

type candidate = {
  doc_id : T.doc_id;
  revision : int;
  contents : string;
  document_hits : int;
  num_hits : int;
  coverage : int;
  mode_offset : int;
  window : T.range;
  range : T.range;
}

let collect_hits db (anchor_norm : normalized) =
  let by_doc = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let query_shingles = ref 0 in
  iter_shingles ~offset:1 anchor_norm.text (fun anchor_offset shingle ->
      incr query_shingles;
      DB.Shingles.find db (Internal_types.Shingle_str.create shingle)
      |> List.iter (fun (doc_id, (range : T.range)) ->
          let hit =
            {
              anchor_offset;
              query_start = anchor_norm.norm_to_raw.(anchor_offset);
              doc_start = range.start;
              doc_end = range.end_;
            }
          in
          let previous =
            Option.value (Hashtbl.find_opt by_doc doc_id) ~default:[]
          in
          Hashtbl.replace by_doc doc_id (hit :: previous)));
  (!query_shingles, by_doc)

(* Count matched query bytes once, even where overlapping shingles agree. *)
let hit_coverage hits =
  let sorted =
    List.sort (fun a b -> Int.compare a.anchor_offset b.anchor_offset) hits
  in
  let _, coverage =
    List.fold_left
      (fun (end_, total) hit ->
        let next_end = hit.anchor_offset + shingle_length in
        (next_end, total + next_end - max end_ hit.anchor_offset))
      (0, 0) sorted
  in
  coverage

(* Count equal raw displacements. Resolve frequency ties by signed offset,
   independently of hash-table iteration order. Hits are nonempty here. *)
let most_common_offset hits =
  let counts = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  List.iter
    (fun hit ->
      let offset = hit.query_start - hit.doc_start in
      let count = Option.value (Hashtbl.find_opt counts offset) ~default:0 in
      Hashtbl.replace counts offset (count + 1))
    hits;
  let offset, _ =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun offset count (best_offset, best_count) ->
        if count > best_count || (count = best_count && offset < best_offset)
        then (offset, count)
        else (best_offset, best_count))
      counts (max_int, 0)
  in
  offset

(* Bytewise alignment may stop inside a UTF-8 character. Realign within the
   narrowed target so the support count describes only the returned bytes. *)
let align_normalized query target =
  let rec align offset target =
    match Util.Smith_waterman.align Util.Smith_waterman.code query target with
    | None -> None
    | Some aligned ->
        let start, end_ =
          Util.Text.safe_range target ~start:aligned.target.start
            ~end_:aligned.target.end_
        in
        if start = aligned.target.start && end_ = aligned.target.end_ then
          Some
            {
              aligned with
              target = { start = offset + start; end_ = offset + end_ };
            }
        else if start >= end_ then None
        else align (offset + start) (String.sub target start (end_ - start))
  in
  align 0 target

let align_candidate ~query ~normalized_query (meta : T.doc_meta) contents hits
    =
  let mode_offset = most_common_offset hits in
  let selected =
    List.filter
      (fun hit ->
        abs (hit.query_start - hit.doc_start - mode_offset)
        <= match_offset_tolerance)
      hits
  in
  let start, end_ =
    List.fold_left
      (fun (start, end_) hit ->
        (min start hit.doc_start, max end_ hit.doc_end))
      (String.length contents, 0)
      selected
  in
  (* Include the query's predicted edges, not just the indexed hits. A name
     change near the beginning can otherwise hide the function header from
     alignment. Local alignment decides which boundary bytes still match. *)
  let start = min start (max 0 (-mode_offset)) in
  let end_ =
    max end_
      (min (String.length contents) (String.length query - mode_offset))
  in
  let window =
    {
      T.start = max 0 (start - shingle_length);
      end_ = min (String.length contents) (end_ + shingle_length);
    }
  in
  let start, end_ =
    Util.Text.safe_range contents ~start:window.start ~end_:window.end_
  in
  let window = { T.start; end_ } in
  (* A normalized shingle may span an arbitrarily long raw whitespace run.
     Enforce the displacement allowance on the whole window before alignment. *)
  let maximum_window =
    String.length query + (2 * match_offset_tolerance) + (2 * shingle_length)
  in
  if window.end_ - window.start > maximum_window then None
  else begin
    let target =
      normalize_whitespace
        (String.sub contents window.start (window.end_ - window.start))
    in
    match align_normalized normalized_query target.text with
    | None -> None
    | Some aligned ->
        let start, end_ =
          Util.Text.raw_range_of_normalized target ~start:aligned.target.start
            ~end_:aligned.target.end_
        in
        let start = window.start + start in
        let end_ = window.start + end_ in
        let minimum_length = (String.length normalized_query + 1) / 2 in
        if aligned.identical_bytes < minimum_length then None
        else
          Some
            {
              doc_id = meta.doc_id;
              revision = meta.revision;
              contents;
              document_hits = List.length hits;
              num_hits = List.length selected;
              coverage = hit_coverage selected;
              mode_offset;
              window;
              range = { T.start; end_ };
            }
  end

let compare_candidates a b =
  let c = Int.compare b.coverage a.coverage in
  if c <> 0 then c
  else
    let c = Int.compare b.num_hits a.num_hits in
    if c <> 0 then c else compare a.doc_id b.doc_id

let find_candidates db query anchor_norm =
  let query_shingles, by_doc = collect_hits db anchor_norm in
  (* Half the unique query shingles, adjusted for the document stride. *)
  let minimum_hits =
    max 1 ((query_shingles + (2 * shingle_offset) - 1) / (2 * shingle_offset))
  in
  let rejected = ref 0 in
  let candidates =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun doc_id hits acc ->
        if List.length hits < minimum_hits then (
          incr rejected;
          acc)
        else
          match DB.Documents.get_full_by_id db doc_id with
          | None ->
              failwith
                (sprintf "anchor relocation error: missing document in db: %s"
                   (App_types.Doc_id.to_string doc_id))
          | Some (_, DB.Deleted) -> acc
          | Some (meta, DB.Active contents) -> (
              match
                align_candidate ~query ~normalized_query:anchor_norm.text meta
                  contents hits
              with
              | None ->
                  incr rejected;
                  acc
              | Some candidate -> candidate :: acc))
      by_doc []
  in
  ( query_shingles,
    minimum_hits,
    !rejected,
    List.sort compare_candidates candidates )

let preview text =

(* Log both snapshots before overwriting the anchor. Filtered documents are
   counted in aggregate rather than logged as relocation candidates. *)
let log_relocation_candidates db (a : Internal_types.anchor) ~doc_revision
    ~anchor_norm ~query_shingles ~minimum_hits ~rejected candidates =
  let document_name doc_id =
    match DB.Documents.get_by_id db doc_id with
    | None -> App_types.Doc_id.to_string doc_id ^ " (missing)"
    | Some meta ->
        sprintf "%s source=%S path=%S revision=%d"
          (App_types.Doc_id.to_string doc_id)
          (App_types.Source.to_string meta.source_doc.source)
          meta.source_doc.locator meta.revision
  in
  let anchor_id = App_types.Anchor_id.to_string a.anchor_id in
  let original = List.find_opt (fun c -> c.doc_id = a.doc_id) candidates in
  let selected = List.nth_opt candidates 0 in
  let name = function
    | None -> "none"
    | Some c -> document_name c.doc_id
  in
  Util.Log.printf
    "Anchor relocation %s before mutation\n\
     original_document=%s original_revision=%d original_range=B%d-%d\n\
     original_text_bytes=%d original_text_preview=%S\n\
     attempt_revision=%d unique_query_shingles=%d minimum_hits=%d \
     candidates=%d filtered_documents=%d\n\
     selection_policy=greatest matched query coverage; ties prefer more \
     inlier hits, then lowest document ID\n\
     original_document_preference=none\n\
     original_document_best=%s selected_destination=%s"
    anchor_id (document_name a.doc_id) a.doc_revision a.range.start
    a.range.end_
    (String.length a.raw_contents)
    (preview a.raw_contents) doc_revision query_shingles minimum_hits
    (List.length candidates) rejected (name original) (name selected);
  List.iteri
    (fun i candidate ->
      let reason =
        if i = 0 then
          "selected: greatest matched query coverage; deterministic tie \
           breaking"
        else "not selected: lower coverage or tie priority"
      in
      Util.Log.printf
        "Anchor relocation %s candidate-%d\n\
         document=%s original_document=%b matching_hits=%d document_hits=%d \
         meets_minimum_hits=true\n\
         coverage_bytes=%d normalized_anchor_bytes=%d coverage_fraction=%.6f\n\
         mode_offset=%d offset_tolerance=%d window=B%d-%d \
         predicted_range=B%d-%d\n\
         reason=%s"
        anchor_id (i + 1)
        (document_name candidate.doc_id)
        (candidate.doc_id = a.doc_id)
        candidate.num_hits candidate.document_hits candidate.coverage
        (String.length anchor_norm.text)
        (float_of_int candidate.coverage
        /. float_of_int (String.length anchor_norm.text))
        candidate.mode_offset match_offset_tolerance candidate.window.start
        candidate.window.end_ candidate.range.start candidate.range.end_
        reason)
    candidates;
  let inspect role = function
    | None -> Util.Log.printf "Anchor relocation %s %s=none" anchor_id role
    | Some c ->
        let text =
          String.sub c.contents c.range.start (c.range.end_ - c.range.start)
        in
        Util.Log.printf
          "Anchor relocation %s %s\n\
           document=%s target_revision=%d effective_range=B%d-%d \
           text_bytes=%d text_truncated=%b text_preview=%S\n\
           would_change_document=%b would_change_range=%b \
           would_change_contents=%b"
          anchor_id role (document_name c.doc_id) c.revision c.range.start
          c.range.end_ (String.length text)
          (String.length text > 2048)
          (preview text) (c.doc_id <> a.doc_id) (c.range <> a.range)
          (text <> a.raw_contents)
  in
  inspect "original_document_candidate" original;
  inspect "selected_destination" selected

(* Failed attempts preserve the old range and contents. The caller owns the
   transaction containing both the document update and anchor relocation. *)
let relocate_one db (a : Internal_types.anchor) ~doc_revision =
  let anchor_norm = normalize_whitespace a.raw_contents in
  let query_shingles, minimum_hits, rejected, candidates =
    find_candidates db a.raw_contents anchor_norm
  in
  log_relocation_candidates db a ~doc_revision ~anchor_norm ~query_shingles
    ~minimum_hits ~rejected candidates;
  match candidates with
  | [] ->
      DB.Anchors.mark_attempt_failed db a.anchor_id
        ~doc_revision_attempt:doc_revision;
      None
  | candidate :: _ ->
      let range = candidate.range in
      let raw_contents =
        String.sub candidate.contents range.start (range.end_ - range.start)
      in
      let changed =
        candidate.doc_id <> a.doc_id
        || range <> a.range
        || raw_contents <> a.raw_contents
      in
      let updated =
        {
          a with
          doc_id = candidate.doc_id;
          doc_revision = candidate.revision;
          doc_revision_attempt = candidate.revision;
          range;
          raw_contents;
          last_author = T.Algo;
        }
      in
      Util.Log.printf
        "Anchor relocation %s applying relocation: document=%s revision=%d \
         range=B%d-%d changed=%b; previous anchor content still intact"
        (App_types.Anchor_id.to_string a.anchor_id)
        (App_types.Doc_id.to_string candidate.doc_id)
        candidate.revision range.start range.end_ changed;
      DB.Anchors.relocate db updated;
      if changed then Some updated else None

(* Borderline cases for the relocation heuristic                        *)
(* -------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* The shingle-based matcher (see Text.ml) is a heuristic, not an exact
   algorithm: it can be wrong in both directions. The tests below don't aim
   to nail down its exact decision boundary (that would over-fit these
   tests to today's [shingle_length]/[shingle_offset]/[min_relocation_hits]
   values, which are meant to be tunable); instead each one demonstrates
   one clear, realistic example of a labeled outcome, so a future change to
   the heuristic has something concrete to check itself against:

   - TRUE POSITIVE: an edit the heuristic is specifically meant to survive
     (see [normalize_whitespace]) does get relocated correctly.
   - TRUE NEGATIVE: an edit that leaves nothing of the original text
     recognizable correctly does NOT get force-relocated onto unrelated
     text of similar shape.
   - FALSE NEGATIVE: a real limitation -- edits small enough, and spread
     out evenly enough, that most of the text survives byte-for-byte, but
     every stored shingle happens to be touched by one of them, so the
     heuristic finds nothing at all.
   - FALSE POSITIVE: another real limitation -- pure text matching can't
     tell a genuine move from a coincidental duplicate, so an anchor whose
     own text was replaced can "relocate" onto an unrelated document that
     happens to share a long verbatim block with the original (e.g.
     boilerplate, a copy-pasted helper, a shared header). *)

  (* Preserve the boundary bytes to isolate whitespace edits in the interior.
     Widen every space between these guards to three spaces. *)
  let widen_interior_spaces s ~guard =
    let n = String.length s in
    let core_start = min guard n in
    let core_end = max core_start (n - guard) in
    let before = String.sub s 0 core_start in
    let core = String.sub s core_start (core_end - core_start) in
    let after = String.sub s core_end (n - core_end) in
    let widened_core = String.concat "   " (String.split_on_char ' ' core) in
    before ^ widened_core ^ after

  (* Replace every [period]-th byte of [s] with [replacement]: a "light"
     edit in the sense that only [1/period] of the bytes change, but
     spread out just densely enough (period <= shingle_offset) that every
     possible [shingle_length]-byte window contains at least one of them.

item.text:
If anchor text matches in multiple files, relocation chooses one candidate automatically. It ranks candidates by matched text coverage, then matching hits, then lowest document ID; it gives the original file no preference. An exact tie can therefore move an anchor to another file for an arbitrary reason. [Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-sitemap/src/skeletor/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:348)

That is deterministic, but generally undesirable: identical text does not establish that the anchor moved. The tests document a case where an unrelated copy of the text is chosen. A safer policy would keep a valid match in the original file and treat unresolved matches across files as ambiguous, requiring review. [Text_api_tests.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-sitemap/src/skeletor/base-libs/text/tests/Text_api_tests.ml:1097)
